question.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-6,-3]\times [1,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=2x{y}^{2}-6x+4{y}^{3}+7. $$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[-6,\,1]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[-3,\,2]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).
${x}_{2}=[$ {{field-1}} $]$
$1.75$
question.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2}-6x+4{y}^{3}+7) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2}-6x+4{y}^{3}+7)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-6 \\ 4xy+12{y}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{y}^{2}-6) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(4xy+12{y}^{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(2{y}^{2}-6) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(4xy+12{y}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 4y \\ 4y & 4x+24y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}0 & 4y \\ 4y & 4x+24y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-6 \\ 4xy+12{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}0 & 4y \\ 4y & 4x+24y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-6 \\ 4xy+12{y}^{2}\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}0 & 4(2) \\ 4(2) & 4(-3)+24(2)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2(2)^{2}-6 \\ 4(-3)(2)+12(2)^{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}0 & 8 \\ 8 & 36\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{0\cdot 36-8\cdot 8}[\begin{aligned}36 & -8 \\ -8 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 24\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{64}[\begin{aligned}-120 \\ -16\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4.875 \\ 1.75\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
